criterion: conformance.report sorts Codex and hook sessions on one comparable value, and _overlaps needs no type filter to avoid inventing an overlap
summary: Clause 1 met: reviewer's own fixture of two Codex rows bracketing a hook session sorts monotonically with all keys str, which the integer form could never do. Clause 2 ruled mis-specified, and explicitly not a redefinition to fit what was built. Reviewer verified the load-bearing facts itself: journal.py:321 validates only `event`; a hand-written month file with an integer ts on a claude session reaches the verdict; replacing the check with the presence-only version the criterion implies makes report() raise TypeError; and there is no separable type filter to delete, because isinstance(value, str) IS the presence check. Provenance settles intent - the phrase is lifted from the pre-node docstring about the two sources - and the discriminator applied was that the surviving check is source-blind: it fired on a forged hook record exactly as on a Codex one, so it is not a guard for two sources, which is what the node objective forbids. Reviewer also named the alternative that would meet the clause literally (validate ts in journal.read) and agreed it is out of this node's scope.
